plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic of a single array drawn as a long horizontal strip of equal cells, shaded to mark off four regions. Four italic labels sit above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the fourth cell, j further to the right, and r over the rightmost cell. Three heavy black bars stand between cells as the region boundaries. The four cells from p through i are pale gray; the six cells between the first and second bar are a darker gray; the five cells after the second bar and before the last are white and empty; and the single cell at the right end, under r, is white and holds the italic letter x. Three curly braces beneath the strip label the pale gray stretch as at most x, written with the symbol for less than or equal to followed by x, the dark gray stretch as greater than x, and the white stretch as unrestricted. The shading separates the portion of the array already classified against the pivot from the portion not yet examined. The strip states the invariant holding at the top of each iteration while a subarray is rearranged in place around the pivot value stored at position r.

interactionPlan.concept: PARTITION maintains a loop invariant: at the top of each iteration A[p..i] holds elements ≤ the pivot x, A[i+1..j−1] holds elements > x, and A[j..r−1] is still unexamined, with x stored at A[r].
elements: single horizontal array strip of 16 equal square cells with thin black borders
italic serif labels p, i, j, r above the strip marking index positions
thick black vertical boundary bars between cells at i, j, and r
pale gray cells (p..i) forming the ≤ x region
darker gray cells (i+1..j−1) forming the > x region
white empty cells (j..r−1) forming the unrestricted region
rightmost cell at r, white, containing the italic letter x (the pivot)
curly brace beneath the ≤ x region labeled '≤ x'
curly brace beneath the > x region labeled '> x'
curly brace beneath the unrestricted region labeled 'unrestricted'
numeric values drawn inside each cell (added for the interactive demo so comparisons are visible)

interactions.label: Implement PARTITION(A, p, r)

api.does: read — returns the current value of A[j]
returns the pivot value x = A[r]
mutate — exchange A[a] and A[b]; the ONLY way to change the array
annotate — attach your own comment to the current frame

interactions.frame: the full strip re-shaded by region (pale gray ≤ x, dark gray > x, white unrestricted), boundary bars at i and j, the pivot cell at r, plus the one or two indices the executed op touched
interactions.success_check: after the loop, there exists a returned index q = i+1 such that A[p..q−1] ≤ x and A[q..r−1] > x, and the strip shows no unrestricted cells remaining

interactions.label: Test case
interactions.teaches: Each iteration's behavior is decided by one comparison: when A[j] ≤ x the code swaps A[i+1] with A[j] and advances both i and j; when A[j] > x only j advances, so the > x region simply absorbs the cell

demo_steps.title: Read the invariant
demo_steps.narration: The strip shows the state at the top of a loop iteration: everything left of bar i is ≤ x, everything between bars i and j is > x, and everything right of j is still unexamined. The pivot x waits at A[r].

demo_steps.title: Run PARTITION step by step
demo_steps.narration: Replay the sample code: each loop iteration compares A[j] to x and re-shades exactly one cell, moving the bars so the pale-gray, dark-gray, and white regions always match the invariant.

demo_steps.title: Flip the comparison
demo_steps.narration: Switch the test case to an A[j] > x array: now the same loop advances j without swapping, showing why one branch moves both bars while the other moves only j.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The invariant does all the work: each iteration classifies A[j] against x once, growing the ≤ x region by a swap or the > x region by default, until every cell is classified and the pivot slides into its final position.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: One long horizontal strip of 16 square cells centered on the canvas, matching the textbook figure's proportions (about 4 pale-gray cells, 6 dark-gray, 5 white, 1 pivot cell). Labels p, i, j, r in large italic serif sit above the strip at their index positions; thick black bars stand vertically between cells at the three boundaries. Curly braces below group the three regions with labels '≤ x', '> x', 'unrestricted' in serif text; the pivot cell shows italic x. For the interactive version, small numerals are drawn inside cells and the region shading plus bar positions are recomputed on every replayed step as i and j advance — shading must read as distinctly pale gray, medium gray, and white at a glance.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Code editor for PARTITION(A, p, r): learner implements the loop using pivot x, indices i and j, compare(A[j], x), and swap primitives; each executed line advances the strip boundaries and updates the <= x, > x, and unrestricted regions.
- Step-through invariant view: before and after every loop iteration, the diagram highlights which cells satisfy the invariant A[p..i] <= x, A[i+1..j-1] > x, and A[j..r-1] unrestricted.
- Test-case toggle: switch the current A[j] between <= x and > x cases to see why one branch swaps and advances i while the other only advances j.

discrepancies: The strip figure is rendered noticeably small relative to the large control panel beside it, so the brace labels (≤ x, > x, unrestricted) and the serif p/i/j/r labels are much smaller than in the source and only marginally comfortable to read at inline size
The braces are thin approximated curves rather than the prominent curly braces of the source, slightly weakening the visual grouping cue

In the source the i/j/r bars are thick black rectangles that clearly interrupt the strip; the generated bars are correct but the j bar position (index 9) leaves a slightly different cell-count split per region than the source's 4/6/5 proportions (minor)
evaluation.notes: The default state faithfully reproduces the CLRS PARTITION loop-invariant strip — 16 cells, correct three-region shading, black i/j/r bars, pivot x at A[r], and braces with ≤x/>x/unrestricted labels — and adds a genuinely functional code-editor workbench with step replay, demo steps, and a test-case toggle that all correctly demonstrate the invariant.
action_items: Increase the strip's size relative to the control panel (larger CELL or wider viewbox share) so the figure reads as the primary element and the brace/index labels match the source's prominent hierarchy
Thicken and deepen the curly braces (stroke width ~2, more pronounced center cusp) to better match the source's grouping brackets
Slightly enlarge the serif p/i/j/r labels and brace labels so they remain legible at inline rendering size

feedback.rationale: No failure modes, concept and geometry are perfect (5s), interactivity fully functional, and the remaining discrepancies are minor polish (strip size, brace thickness) on an already faithful figure — overall average 4.6 indicates diminishing returns from further iteration.
